A modern, well-established medical centre in Cranbourne West, Victoria, is seeking a vocationally registered (VR) General Practitioner to join its busy, doctor-led practice. Operating under a bulk-billing model, this clinic prioritizes comprehensive, patient-centered care alongside highly sustainable workloads. The facility boasts a collaborative, low-ego team culture where absolute clinical autonomy is respected. The incoming practitioner will benefit from a robust on-site multidisciplinary network, which includes existing general practitioners, a dentist, seven-day pathology, and access to specialists in cardiology, pediatrics, and gastroenterology. 

 The practice is fully equipped with modern consulting rooms, state-of-the-art systems like Best Practice software, Tyro EFTPOS, and HICAPS, as well as ample on-site parking. To minimize non-clinical administrative burdens, comprehensive support is provided by a dedicated team of nurses, administrative staff, allied health professionals, and an experienced practice manager. This includes robust assistance with Chronic Disease Management (CDM), allowing the incoming doctor to focus entirely on high-quality care. For those looking to expand their professional scope, the clinic offers diverse opportunities to pursue special interests, engage in continuing professional development (CPD), and take on supervisor roles within the practice. 

 Recognizing the importance of work-life balance, this position offers flexible consulting hours with full-time, part-time, or contractor arrangements available across weekdays, after-hours, and weekends. Located in a thriving, accessible community (classified as an MMM-1 location), the role delivers excellent lifestyle benefits alongside strong financial rewards. The successful candidate will step into a highly lucrative environment with an established patient base, supported by an initial guaranteed rate of $220 per hour for the first three months, or 70% of billings (whichever is greater). Applicants must hold AHPRA registration, FRACGP/FACRRM qualifications (or be actively working towards fellowship), and a current Medicare provider number.   Apply Now

 Apply now
 Job no: 944552

 Work type: Full time

 Categories: Administration, Business and Management





 

Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network
 

Rural and Remote Mental Health - Parkside 

Salary: ASO5 $92,122 - $102,456 per annum

Full-Time, Temporary up to 8th January 2028 

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

The Administration Manager provides leadership and coordination of administrative services across the Rural and Remote Mental Health Service, and Barossa Hills Fleurieu Community Mental Health Team (CMHTs), ensuring the delivery of efficient, high-quality day-to-day operations including workforce planning, rostering, recruitment and performance management. It plays a key role in fostering a positive, customer-focused team culture while providing strategic HR and operational support across onboarding, staff development, workforce administration and compliance, and driving ongoing improvement in systems, processes and service delivery.

The position contributes to effective governance and strong business operations through committee coordination, reporting and capital processes, working collaboratively with senior leaders, clinicians and stakeholders to support integrated service delivery. It also supports budget monitoring, operational and workforce planning, funding submissions, quality improvement activities and project work, while assisting with high-quality reporting and responses to enquiries and consumer matters.

WHO ARE WE? 

The Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network offers opportunities across our sites, from Kangaroo Island to Eudunda, wrapping all the way around our metropolitan areas. We pride ourselves on providing exceptional care to all our consumers, residents, their families, and community. Our mission is to ensure that you always receive the best quality, safe, consistent, collaborative care and always with kindness. We do this by maintaining exceptional levels of care at all times supported by systems and processes that assure us of quality and safety of our staff and those we serve.

WHERE AND HOW YOU WILL WORK 

Parkside, South Australia is a well-located inner-southern suburb just minutes from Adelaide's CBD, known for its leafy streets, convenient transport options, and easy access to local caf s, parks, and everyday amenities.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 

How do you build effective working relationships and communicate with a wide range of stakeholders across an organisation?

Are you motivated to lead and inspire a high-performing administrative team in a dynamic healthcare environment? 

Do you take pride in delivering efficient, high-quality services while continuously improving systems and processes? 

Are you driven to build strong, collaborative relationships with leaders, clinicians and stakeholders to achieve shared goals? 

Do you thrive on planning, organising and coordinating workforce and operational priorities in a fast-paced setting? 

Are you committed to maintaining high standards of governance, accountability and customer-focused service delivery?

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

You will....

Lead and coordinate the delivery of administrative services across mental health programs 

Oversee workforce planning, rostering, recruitment and performance management 

Manage HR processes including onboarding, staff development and compliance 

Support governance through reporting, committee coordination and business operations 

Contribute to planning, budgeting, quality improvement and project activities

WHAT WILL WE OFFER YOU IN RETURN? 

At BHFLHN, not only will you be working in an environment surrounded by beautiful scenery and nature we see your work here as not just as a job, but an opportunity to extend, progress or consolidate your career with us. We therefore offer you opportunities to be supported in the following ways:

Salary package a range of benefits (including living expenses such as mortgage, rent, utility bills and groceries) up to $9,010 each FBT year + $2,650 for Meal Entertainment expenses each FBT yearClick here more information

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities.

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program.

Health and Fitness Benefits: Access to Fitness Passport, a discounted workplace health and fitness program available to BHFLHN staff and their families.

WHAT ELSE DO YOU NEED TO KNOW-WHAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR SUCCESS? 

Working in this environment, it is important to us that we only employ people with the upmost integrity and commitment to serving the South Australian community and its visitors to the highest possible standards. To ensure that we meet that commitment there are a few checks that you will be required to undertake. These are detailed on the Role Description, but are likely to include the following:

You will need to be immunised. Please contact the Enquiries Person for this position if you have any queries. Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy.Further information is in the application for to help guide you. 

You will need to undergo employment screening, what you require is also on the front page of the Role Description.

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY & INCLUSION 

We employ people as diverse as the clients we support and the environments we work in. At BHFLHN we pride ourselves on being an Equal Opportunity employer committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees and therefore we encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, disability, all genders, and LGBTQI+ community. We continually look for ways to support and promote diversity and flexible ways of working so please let us know what interests you.

 Department of Health

 People & Culture

Position details

Health and Human Services (Tasmanian State Service) Award, General Stream, Band 3

Fixed-term, full-time, Permanent, full-time

North, South

 

 
 

 
Job description:

 
Join an evolving recruitment team to provide high-quality, end-to-end recruitment support, working closely with hiring managers and stakeholders to deliver efficient and effective recruitment outcomes across the Department of Health.

 

 






 

The Team

Recruitment Services is implementing a new statewide operating model and structure designed to strengthen recruitment capability, improve consistency, and support a more modern end-to-end service across the Department of Health. We're building a stronger, more specialised team to support consistent end-to-end recruitment across the Department, and we're recruiting to multiple roles as part of this implementation.

Why this is a great time to join

You'll join an evolving, statewide team that is improving how recruitment works in practice - standardising workflows, lifting capability, and using technology more effectively to support managers and candidates. This is an opportunity to have real impact at scale, contribute to continuous improvement, and help attract the workforce that supports health services across Tasmania, leading to stronger Tasmanian community. 

The Role

As a Recruitment Officer, you will support the end-to-end recruitment process by:

Engaging with stakeholders with a client and customer focus, providing timely and friendly support.

Coordinating recruitment administration activities from advertising through to appointment.

Maintaining accurate and confidential records within e-Recruitment and HR systems.

Monitoring recruitment workflows and assisting the team to meet service delivery timeframes.

Responding to recruitment enquiries and providing advice through the People and Culture Portal.

Preparing and distributing recruitment and selection documentation.

Drafting applicant communications and ensuring candidates receive timely updates.

Publishing job advertisements across approved recruitment platforms.

Processing establishment changes and minor position amendments.

Supporting continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance recruitment processes and services.

Providing general administrative support to the Recruitment team as required.

You will need

Knowledge of, and-or experience within a human resources or recruitment operational environment and in the use of human resource management systems, applicant tracking systems, technical tools or databases particularly in the areas of recruitment or demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Knowledge of, and experience in the application of recruitment practices, procedures and legislation or a demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Well-developed interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain operational procedures and provide information to, and liaise with, clients, stakeholders and members of the public.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Details of appointment

Permanent full time, day worker position, working 76 hours per fortnight.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$76,849 to $82,996 per annum. Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with the Health and Human Services (Tasmanian State Service) Award (HAHSA) and the Public Sector Union Wages Agreement (PSUWA).

Benefits available to eligible candidates 

A range of leave entitlements, access to additional leave incentives, generous personal leave, including family incentives, purchased leave options.

Workplace flexibility aligned our flexible work policy.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

Carer Employer Accreditation, evidencing our commitment to supporting employees with caring responsibilities. (Find out more under the Carer Recognition Act 2023).

More information about our Employee Benefits can be found here

Eligibility

We encourage you to review the Statement of Duties, Applicant Guide, prior to applying for an overview of the duties, program, selection process and application guidance.

Recruitment Officer Band 3 (word)

Applicant Guide.docx

How to apply

Apply Online. Please click the "Apply" button on this screen to ensure that important questions about you are answered.

You will be prompted to complete a 1-2 page application detailing your experience, skills and knowledge as they relate to the attached Statement of Duties. A separate statement addressing the selection criteria in the Statement of Duties is not required.

For more information

Applicants who require further information are encouraged to contact the Contact person for detailed information about the vacancy.

Allison Hanson - Manager - Recruitment - 0416 516 016 - allison.hanson@health.tas.gov.au

WHAT ARE WE OFFERING? 

Join our People and Culture team as a Recruitment Specialist and play a key role in delivering best-practice recruitment, selection and onboarding services across the network. In this dynamic position, you will provide expert advice and consultancy to managers and selection panels, ensuring recruitment processes are fair, compliant, efficient and aligned with contemporary workforce practices. You will support a broad range of recruitment activities, including large-scale campaigns, international recruitment, visa and relocation processes, stakeholder engagement, and the effective use of e-recruitment systems. Working closely with leaders and business units, you will help attract and secure high-quality talent while delivering an exceptional candidate and hiring manager experience. 

This role offers the opportunity to lead innovative recruitment projects, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute to workforce planning and talent attraction strategies. You will analyse recruitment data, identify opportunities to enhance processes and customer service, develop and deliver recruitment training programs, and collaborate with key stakeholders to implement modern recruitment solutions across the organisation. If you are a proactive human resources professional with strong consultancy skills, a passion for innovation, and a commitment to delivering outstanding recruitment outcomes, this is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful impact. 

WHO ARE WE? 

The Barossa Hills Fleurieu Local Health Network offers opportunities across our sites, from Kangaroo Island to Eudunda, wrapping all the way around our metropolitan areas. We pride ourselves on providing exceptional care to all our consumers, residents, their families, and community. Our mission is to ensure that you always receive the best quality, safe, consistent, collaborative care and always with kindness. We do this by maintaining exceptional levels of care at all times supported by systems and processes that assure us of quality and safety of our staff and those we serve.

In this role you will be required to work in our Regional Offices in the Adelaide CBD 2 - 3 days per week and enjoy working from home or from one of our many sites on other days of the week - flexibility is offered in regard to what days you work in the city to assist you in creating a work-life balance. Enjoy the flexibility of being mobile whilst supporting our sites across our region.

Do you have a passion for attracting, engaging and securing high-quality talent through contemporary recruitment and selection practices? 

Are you commited to delivering exceptional customer service, building trusted relationships and providing professional advice to managers, candidates and stakeholders? 

Can you identify opportunities for innovation, continuous improvement and process optimisation to enhance recruitment outcomes and efficiency? 

Do you have great communication, influencing and consultancy skills, with the confidence to guide and support stakeholders through complex recruitment matters? 

Are you proactive, solutions-focused with the ability to lead projects, manage competing priorities and drive positive workforce outcomes in a fast-paced environment? 

If you have answered yes to any of these questions - then read on. 

HOW WILL YOU CONTRIBUTE? 

In this role you will..... 

lead and coordinate end-to-end recruitment, selection and onboarding processes while ensuring compliance with legislation, policies and best-practice workforce standards. 

provide expert advice and consultancy to managers and selection panels on recruitment strategies, merit-based selection, talent attraction and workforce planning initiatives. 

manage large-scale and specialised recruitment campaigns, including international recruitment, visa and relocation processes, to attract and secure high-quality talent. 

identify opportunities for continuous improvement by analysing recruitment data, reviewing processes and implementing innovative solutions that enhance service delivery and candidate experience 

develop and deliver training, resources and recruitment projects that build stakeholder capability and maximise the use of contemporary recruitment tools and e-recruitment systems.

Access to generous leave provisions and professional development opportunities. 

Support for you and your family via our free Employee Assistance Program.
